summary: Helper C extension adds SHA-256 build_id, peer-identity-authenticated capability store, and 5 new methods (client.open, register-owned, terminate-owned, release-owned, helper.restart). CommandJobManager.cancel() now consults the helper ONLY on EPERM (helperOwnedPgidProvider DI seam). Cross-client isolation enforced by token+peer(UID+PID) matching. PID reuse resistance via kinfo_proc.kp_proc.p_un.__p_starttime. Helper termination policy is fixed (TERM -> grace -> KILL), not caller-controlled. 65 helper unit tests pass; 10/10 supervised-shell tests pass.

review_correction01.trigger: Expert review of the original ACT identified 3 P0 invariants + 2 P1 hygiene issues that the v1 implementation did not satisfy.

P0-1_ownership_proof.defect: Original register-owned checked only (leader_uid == peer_uid). Any same-UID process could register any same-UID process group it did NOT spawn (the naked PGID killer).
P0-1_ownership_proof.fix: Added read_proc_identity_ext() that reads kp_eproc.e_ppid from sysctl. handle_register_owned now requires (leader_ppid == pi.pid) OR (proposed_pgid == pi.pid). The leader must be the peer's child, or the peer itself.
P0-1_ownership_proof.test: PGID-11 (source: leader_ppid AND kp_eproc.e_ppid referenced AND leader_ppid != pi.pid check exists); PGID-10 (source: PPID check + 2x DENY_OWNERSHIP return points for defence in depth). Runtime: PGID-06 (PID 1 -> DENY_OWNERSHIP).

P0-2_fail_closed_peer_pid.defect: Original peer_identity() returned ok=1 with pid=0 if LOCAL_PEERPID failed. Multiple same-UID clients would collapse onto (uid=501, pid=0) defeating cross-client isolation.
P0-2_fail_closed_peer_pid.fix: LOCAL_PEERPID is now mandatory. getsockopt < 0 returns pi without setting ok. Defensive ppid <= 0 also fails closed. handle_register_owned rejects pi.pid <= 0 with PEER_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE.
P0-2_fail_closed_peer_pid.test: PGID-12 (source: getsockopt<0 returns pi WITHOUT setting ok AND ppid<=0 fails closed).

P0-3_request_id_correlation_on_success.defect: handle_terminate_owned and handle_release_owned success envelopes did not echo request_id, causing the TS HelperClient to throw RequestIdMismatchError on every successful terminate/release.
P0-3_request_id_correlation_on_success.fix: Both handlers now use write_json_string(rid->val, rid->val_len) to emit request_id in their success envelopes. Also added INTERNAL_TRUNCATION error path to handle_client_open.
P0-3_request_id_correlation_on_success.test: PGID-13 (source: handle_release_owned uses write_json_string + request_id + RELEASED); PGID-14 (source: request_id appears within 500 chars of TERMINATED_TERM AND RELEASED).

P1-1_embedded_build_id.defect: build_id was computed at startup by reading helper.c via $CLINEMM_HELPER_SRC env var. The production binary lives at ~/.clinemm/bin/ not in the repo, so the runtime fallback path could trigger.
P1-1_embedded_build_id.fix: build.sh and Makefile compute SHA-256(ABI_version || helper.c) at build time and pass -DCLINEMM_HELPER_BUILD_ID=... The runtime $CLINEMM_HELPER_SRC fallback path is preserved for tests but wrapped in #ifndef CLINEMM_HELPER_BUILD_ID.
P1-1_embedded_build_id.test: PGID-15 (source: CLINEMM_HELPER_BUILD_ID used AND #ifdef block does NOT call getenv); runtime: ./build.sh and make both produce the SAME embedded build_id ea6256c311a0337df4f0c00cb86e6be05df8f59d7dd08b5c5033a6513b684415.

P1-2_compiler_warnings_as_errors.defect: Makefile/build.sh used -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration to suppress what should be a hard error for a security-sensitive native helper.
P1-2_compiler_warnings_as_errors.fix: Both flags removed. Forward declarations added for read_proc_identity_ext, peer_identity, alloc_client_slot, alloc_job_slot, etc.
P1-2_compiler_warnings_as_errors.test: PGID-16 (CFLAGS line in Makefile does not contain -Wno-... AND build.sh $CC invocation line does not contain -Wno-...). Build is warning-free: cc -O2 -Wall -Wextra helper.c produces zero diagnostics.

review_correction02.context: Post-correction01 the expert surfaced two new load-bearing defects: (1) the HelperOwnedPgidProvider had no production composition path (it was an injectable option but nothing constructed and passed it to CommandJobManager in production), and (2) alloc_*_slot() only inspected the `used` flag, but release/terminate paths only cleared `active`, so the helper would exhaust its 128-slot job pool (and 64-slot client pool) over its entire lifetime.

HALT_HELPER_CAPABILITY_NOT_PRODUCTION_WI.defect: HelperOwnedPgidProvider was an opaque option on CommandJobManager but the production vscode-session-host.ts constructor never built or passed one. The C helper was excellent but unreachable: the actual product path was direct terminateTree -> EPERM -> provider absent -> no LaunchAgent fallback.
HALT_HELPER_CAPABILITY_NOT_PRODUCTION_WI.fix: New file apps/vscode/src/sdk/host-helper-pgid-adapter.ts implements a narrow AF_UNIX wire client + HostHelperPgidProvider class that adapts wire shapes (client_token, job_token, TERMINATED_TERM, RELEASED) to the opaque HelperOwnedPgidProvider interface. resolveLiveHelperOwnedPgidProvider() reads CLINEMM_HOST_HELPER_SOCKET (the canonical env var the Seatbelt backend already type-checks) and returns a live provider, or undefined when unset (non-mac, helper not installed). vscode-session-host.ts now passes helperOwnedPgidProvider: resolveLiveHelperOwnedPgidProvider() into CommandJobManager. The wire client enforces the same anti-shell forbidden-keys guard as the broader client.
HALT_HELPER_CAPABILITY_NOT_PRODUCTION_WI.tests: host-helper-pgid-adapter.test.ts (11 tests, all passing): token-mapping through adapter, terminate success -> { ok: true, outcome }, terminate failure -> { ok: false, code } with DENY_PEER_MISMATCH/TERMINATION_FAILED codes extracted from wire errors, clientOpen failure -> METHOD_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_TS_FALLBACK, release best-effort swallows errors, resolveLiveHelperOwnedPgidProvider returns undefined when env unset, full production-seam test exercising clientOpen -> registerOwned -> terminateOwned flow.

HALT_HELPER_JOB_SLOT_EXHAUSTION.defect: alloc_job_slot() / alloc_client_slot() only check `used`. Successful registration sets used=1 and active=1; release/terminate only clear active. The slot is never reclaimed, so the helper could register at most CLINEMM_MAX_JOBS=128 jobs and CLINEMM_MAX_CLIENTS=64 clients over its ENTIRE lifetime, even after every slot's active flag had been cleared.
HALT_HELPER_JOB_SLOT_EXHAUSTION.fix: Added clear_job_slot() and clear_client_slot() helpers in helper.c that secure-zero the token bytes + identifier fields and set used=0. Called from: (a) handle_release_owned success path, (b) handle_terminate_owned on every terminal branch (ESRCH-on-TERM, TERM-grace, ESRCH-on-KILL, KILL-grace, stale-PID, stale-PGID, TERMINATION_FAILED), (c) new handle_client_close handler that authenticates peer then reclaims the client slot (mirrors the load-bearing fail-closed peer_matches guard from P0-2). The truncation path deliberately does NOT reclaim (client may retry). Added 'client.close' method to the dispatcher and to the TS client/protocol. Test helper.test.ts restartHelperWithEnv() called at the start of new live tests (PGID-19, PGID-21) so the helper is alive after PGID-08 killed it.
HALT_HELPER_JOB_SLOT_EXHAUSTION.tests: PGID-17 (source: handle_release_owned calls clear_job_slot AND does NOT use the old job->active=0 pattern); PGID-18 (source: handle_terminate_owned calls clear_job_slot at least 5 times for the success+stale branches AND does NOT use the old pattern); PGID-19 (live: register+release cycle repeated >128 times does NOT return CAPACITY; the bun test process itself is the leader so no signal is sent); PGID-20 (source: handle_client_close AND clear_client_slot AND strcmp dispatch entry exist); PGID-21 (live: client.open + client.close + client.open produces a different second token, proving slot reuse).

review_correction03.context: Post-correction02 the expert surfaced three P0s: (1) the load-bearing 'production seam' test did NOT actually drive CommandJobManager — it called provider methods directly; (2) the HelperOwnedPgidProvider interface had no clientClose method, so CommandJobManager.dispose() could not reclaim the helper's per-instance client slot (every VS Code instance would leak one slot of the 64-slot pool); (3) three TypeScript errors in command-job-manager.ts — pgid type, epermDetected on TerminateTreeResult, helperClientTokenPromise type — were ACT-owned (introduced by corrections 01/02), not pre-existing.

HALT_PRODUCTION_SEAM_TEST_DOES_NOT_EXERC.defect: The correction02 'production seam' test at host-helper-pgid-adapter.test.ts constructed a CommandJobManager but then called provider.clientOpen / registerOwned / terminateOwned directly. manager.start, manager.cancel, runTerminationSequence, and the epermDetected branch were never exercised. The test even acknowledged it 'simulated' the path.
HALT_PRODUCTION_SEAM_TEST_DOES_NOT_EXERC.fix: Rewrote the production seam test to drive the real manager public seam: (a) new `spawnFactory` test option on CommandJobManagerOptions (correction03) overrides spawnSupervisableShellCommand so the test does not need a real subprocess — a fake long-running process with a synthetic pid is injected; (b) new `epermProbe` test option overrides the default EPERM-on-group-signal probe (which calls process.kill(-pgid, 'SIGTERM')) so the test deterministically takes the helper-fallback branch. The new test asserts: start(state=running) -> cancel(ok=true) -> wire.terminateOwned called exactly once with matching clientToken/jobToken. Two additional tests cover the negative cases: cancel-without-EPERM does NOT consult the helper (EPERM-only fallback invariant), and dispose() reclaims the helper client slot (calls wire.clientClose).
HALT_PRODUCTION_SEAM_TEST_DOES_NOT_EXERC.tests: host-helper-pgid-adapter.test.ts (now 13 tests, all passing — was 11): 5 new tests in the 'real manager seam' describe block. The test fixture includes a `fakeLongRunningProcess()` helper that builds a synthetic SupervisableShellProcess whose pid is in a non-OS range (90_000_000-99_000_000) so it cannot collide with a real OS pid, whose exit promise resolves on terminateTree, and whose terminateTree returns the real TerminateTreeResult shape.

HALT_CLIENT_SLOT_RECLAMATION_NOT_PRODUCT.defect: The C helper's client.close handler was added in correction02, the standalone TS client exposes clientClose — but HelperOwnedPgidProvider (the opaque interface CommandJobManager consumes) had no clientClose method. CommandJobManager.dispose() could not reclaim the helper's per-instance client slot, so every VS Code / Codium instance would leak one slot of the 64-slot client pool.
HALT_CLIENT_SLOT_RECLAMATION_NOT_PRODUCT.fix: Added `clientClose(clientToken: string): Promise<void>` to the HelperOwnedPgidProvider interface (the same opaque interface the manager consumes). Added the wire method to HelperWireClient (calls helper's `client.close` envelope). Added the adapter method on HostHelperPgidProvider (best-effort: catches wire errors). CommandJobManager.dispose() now calls provider.clientClose(this.helperClientToken) after the active-job termination loop, then clears helperClientToken and helperClientTokenPromise. The dispose path is gated on `this.helperClientToken` being set (no provider / no clientOpen = no-op).
HALT_CLIENT_SLOT_RECLAMATION_NOT_PRODUCT.tests: host-helper-pgid-adapter.test.ts: 'real manager seam: dispose() reclaims the helper client slot (clientClose)' — drives manager.start with the fake spawn, cancels the job, then disposes; asserts wire.clientOpen called once and wire.clientClose called once with the matching clientToken. 'real manager seam: dispose() without provider does not call clientClose' — sanity guard: dispose() with no provider must not throw.

HALT_ACT_OWNED_TYPECHECK_ERRORS.defect: Three TypeScript errors in command-job-manager.ts introduced by corrections 01/02: (a) helperClientTokenPromise typed as Promise<string> but .catch() returns undefined; (b) tryRegisterOwnedJob expected childProcess.pgid but SupervisableShellProcess only exposes pid; (c) treeResult.epermDetected read but TerminateTreeResult type only has treeTerminated and escalatedToKill (no epermDetected field on the SDK primitive).
HALT_ACT_OWNED_TYPECHECK_ERRORS.fix: (a) helperClientTokenPromise type widened to `Promise<string | undefined>`. (b) tryRegisterOwnedJob parameter changed from `{readonly pgid?: number}` to `{readonly pid?: number}`; on POSIX, spawnSupervisableShellCommand uses detached:true so the child is its own process-group leader (`pgid === pid`) — this was the implicit assumption, now explicit. Removed the `pgid: undefined` field from the synthetic-process Object.freeze at buildSandboxUnavailableResult (SupervisableShellProcess has no such field). (c) Removed the `epermDetected: false` field from the synthetic process (same reason); added `defaultEpermProbe(pgid)` module-level function that calls process.kill(-pgid, 'SIGTERM') and returns true iff the kernel returned EPERM. Added `epermProbe?: (pgid: number) => boolean` test seam to CommandJobManagerOptions so tests can drive the EPERM branch deterministically without a foreign-UID process group. The runtime probe is harmless: a successful kill actually delivers SIGTERM, which is what the upcoming terminateTree would do anyway — the probe only observes the kernel's response.

Existing command-job-manager.test.ts still 18/20 (pre-existing environment issue: macOS sandboxing prevents bun from process.kill-ing spawned children — verified identical on stashed main, not caused by correction03).

review_correction04.context: Post-correction03 the expert surfaced two P0s: (a) HALT_CORRECTION03_CONTRACT_SPLIT — the manager had a parallel `process.kill(-pgid, "SIGTERM")` probe for EPERM detection, while the SDK bash.ts had already wired `pgid` + `epermDetected` into SupervisableShellProcess / TerminateTreeResult. The root cause was that I added `pgid` + `epermDetected` to the SDK source in this same ACT but never rebuilt `dist/`, so my typecheck ran against stale dist/ and reported 'no pgid / no epermDetected'. I then layered a parallel EPERM seam on top of the (already-correct) source contract. (b) HALT_ARTIFACT_NOT_BOUND_TO_SUBJECT — only the evidence/adapter subset was staged; command-job-manager.ts, vscode-session-host.ts, bash.ts, the helper C, protocol/client changes, etc. remained unstaged, so a commit of the staged state would preserve the closure claim without preserving the implementation.

HALT_CORRECTION03_CONTRACT_SPLIT.defect: CommandJobManager had a parallel `defaultEpermProbe(pgid)` that called `process.kill(-pgid, "SIGTERM")` and returned true on EPERM. Node's `process.kill()` is documented as a signal sender, not an observational probe — it actually delivers the signal. The manager thus issued a DUPLICATE SIGTERM (the upcoming `terminateTree` would have sent the same signal anyway) and read its OWN EPERM, in addition to the SDK primitive's own EPERM observation. Two competing EPERM authorities in the same termination sequence.
HALT_CORRECTION03_CONTRACT_SPLIT.fix: Removed the parallel seam entirely: `defaultEpermProbe()`, `epermProbe` test seam, `probeEpermOnOwnedGroup`, and the constructor wiring. Restored the canonical SDK contract: `tryRegisterOwnedJob` now reads `childProcess.pgid` (the field added in this same ACT to `SupervisableShellProcess`); `runTerminationSequence` now reads `treeResult.epermDetected` (the field added in this same ACT to `TerminateTreeResult`). Rebuilt `@cline/core` dist via `bun --production -F @cline/core build` so the typecheck + tests run against the rebuilt artifacts (not stale dist). Restored the synthetic-process shape to include `pgid: undefined` and `epermDetected: false` (these fields now exist on the rebuilt types).
HALT_CORRECTION03_CONTRACT_SPLIT.tests: host-helper-pgid-adapter.test.ts: fakeLongRunningProcess now takes `opts.epermDetected` and exposes both `pid` + `pgid` fields on the synthetic SupervisableShellProcess. The production-seam test passes `epermDetected: true` so the manager takes the helper-fallback branch via the SDK's canonical diagnostic. The negative test (cancel-without-EPERM) passes `epermDetected: false` and asserts the helper is NOT consulted. 13/13 adapter tests pass; tsc --noEmit 0 errors; no `epermProbe` references remain.

review_correction04.single_eperm_authority_invariant: There is exactly ONE EPERM authority in the system: `SupervisableShellProcess.terminateTree` in `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/executors/bash.ts`. It owns the signaling (signalGroup → process.kill(-childPid, signal)) AND the EPERM observation (returns TerminateTreeResult.epermDetected). CommandJobManager.runTerminationSequence consumes that single field and gates the helper fallback on it. No parallel seam anywhere.
review_correction04.single_pgid_authority_invariant: There is exactly ONE PGID source: `SupervisableShellProcess.pgid` (POSIX-only; undefined on Windows). CommandJobManager.tryRegisterOwnedJob reads it directly and passes it to `provider.registerOwned({ pgid })`. The helper verifies `getpgid(pgid) === pgid` plus UID match before minting a job_token. No `pid === pgid` reconstruction anywhere.
